subject: ACME pricing & invoice estimate — post-discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: ACME pricing & invoice estimate — post-discovery follow-up

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for taking time today — good conversation and helpful context on your expected usage patterns. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Summary of needs: 5k concurrent users for chat assistant (mostly short prompts, avg 40 tokens/request), nightly batch embedding job for ~10M documents/month, and a requirement for audit logs + retention for 12 months.
- Key constraints you mentioned: target unit economics ~ $900-$1,200 / 1M tokens, procurement prefers a single invoice per month, and budget band of $60k–$120k ARR for this initial phase.

Attached is an initial invoice-style estimate and a token-cost model that maps your volumes to per-token unit costs and shows options for dedicated vs hosted routing. See attachments: ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Estimate_v1.xlsx (cost + invoice layout) and ACME_token_cost_model_v2.csv (detailed token math).

Can you confirm the following so we can lock an updated estimate?
1) Monthly token volume (total generated + input) for chat (approx avg tokens per session × daily active sessions).
2) Whether the batch embeddings are 10M distinct documents or 10M embedding requests (affects cache).
3) Any legal/PO constraints we should know for billing (billing address, PO cadence).

If helpful I can send a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet line by line.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0142

Attachments: ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Estimate_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), ACME_token_cost_model_v2.csv (csv)

From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME pricing & invoice estimate — post-discovery follow-up

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the recap and the attachments — looks good as a starting point. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Chat tokens: we estimate ~120M tokens/month initially (this includes both input + output). That assumes ~60k sessions/day, avg 40 tokens per request, ~2 requests/session.
- Embeddings: the 10M figure is distinct documents (we batch process nightly, many will be cached).
- Budget: procurement signaled target of $100k ARR for the pilot, with room up to $150k if performance is demonstrably better than our on-prem solution.
- PO/Billing: procurement prefers monthly invoicing, net 30. Billing address is 123 Enterprise Rd, Boston, MA.

Looping in procurement for PO cadence — Procurement, can you confirm any required invoice fields or PO number format?

Appreciate the quick turnaround. If you can send an updated estimate aligned to 120M tokens/mo and the $/1M token target, that would be great.

Best,
Emily Carter
Director, Product — Chat AI | Acme Corp
emily.carter@acme.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acme.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Revised invoice estimate and cost model (based on 120M tokens/mo)

Emily / team,

Thanks — I updated the cost model and invoice mock to reflect the 120M tokens/month chat load and 10M distinct embedding docs. Key notes in the attached: 

- Two pricing paths included: Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) and Dedicated (monthly reserved capacity). For the pilot volume, Dedicated with a small reserved pool + autoscaling reduces per-1M token cost by ~18% compared to pure hosted.
- Line-item callouts: streaming tokens vs non-streaming, embedding compute, KV cache credits for repeated doc hits, and audit log ingestion (charged as per-MB retained).
- Target unit economics: I modeled $1,050 / 1M tokens in the hosted scenario and $860 / 1M tokens in the dedicated+cache scenario (both before discounts). With your $100k ARR target, the dedicated path gets you closer to the goal once we assume 3–6 month commit.

I've attached: ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Estimate_v1.xlsx (updated) and ACME_token_cost_model_v2.csv (updated with per-path breakdown). Also added a simple mutual action plan (ACME_mutual_action_plan.docx) outlining milestones to procurement + security review.

Next steps I propose: 
- Scheduling a 30-min walkthrough with Emily + Procurement to agree invoice layout and finalize PO requirements.
- Drafting a one-page SOW/engagement sheet for the pilot (we can attach to PO).

If that works, Sean — can you propose two times tomorrow morning?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Estimate_v1.xlsx, ACME_token_cost_model_v2.csv, ACME_mutual_action_plan.docx

From: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>

Cc: Emily Carter <emily.carter@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revised invoice estimate and cost model (based on 120M tokens/mo)

Hi Monica / Sean,

Procurement here — thanks for the update. A few administrative items we need for the invoice/PO: 
- Invoice must include: company legal name (Acme Corporation), billing address (123 Enterprise Rd, Boston, MA), TAX ID, and a single-line description of services referencing our internal project code ACME-AI-2027.
- PO cadence: Monthly invoices, net 30. We use PO numbers in this format ACME-PO-YYYY-####.
- For signature/contracting, please send an engagement SOW and the final invoice mock as PDF. DocuSign link preferred.

We'll prepare an initial PO once we have the SOW and a final invoice layout.

Thanks,
Acme Procurement
procurement@acme.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Rachel and I will draft a one-page SOW and convert the invoice mock to PDF with the required fields (legal name, billing address, TAX ID, and project code). I'll also drop a DocuSign link once ready.

Emily — once you confirm time we'll lock it and I'll send a calendar invite.
